newsitem.title: USA: Paramount wins copyright ruling on photo spoof.
newsitem.headline: Paramount wins copyright ruling on photo spoof.

text.p: A federal judge has thrown out a copyright infringement lawsuit against Viacom Inc.'s Paramount Pictures brought by Annie Leibovitz over a spoof of her famous nude photo of pregnant actress Demi Moore.

U.S. District Judge Loretta Preska, in a ruling made public Thursday, found that Paramount's ad for a "Naked Gun" film featuring comic actor Leslie Nielsen's face superimposed over a pregnant body did not infringe on Leibovitz's copyrighted photo.

In her ruling, dated Thursday, Preska found that Paramount's ad was a parody and a fair use of the copyrighted work that had appeared on the cover of Vanity Fair magazine. She dismissed Leibovitz's argument that the ad was not a parody because it did not comment upon or criticize the Moore photograph.
"The Nielsen ad clearly takes satiric aim directly at the Moore photograph. From the outset, it was intended to make a mockery of an image that becmae a 'cultural icon'," Preska wrote.
"In fact, without reference to the Moore photograph, the Nielsen ad simply is not very funny," she wrote.

Preska said that like all parodies, the ad "relies for its comic effect on the contrast between the original -- a beautiful woman taking great pride in the majesty of her pregnant body -- and the new work -- a ridiculous image of a smirking, foolish-looking pregnant man."
The ad, which was used for the release of "Naked Gun: The Final Insult 33-1/3," shows Nielsen wearing a smirk, and underneath the photo ran the legend "Due This March."
